blocks.value: Logical expressions in Java are evaluated using an efficient algorithm: **short-circuit evaluation**. The computer evaluates a logical expression from left to right and stops as soon as the value of the expression is determined. `&&` and `||` are short-circuit operators, and do not necessarily evaluate all of their operands.

items: Evaluation **stops**. The entire expression returns `false` without ever evaluating `c == d`, because `&&` requires both operands to be true.

Short-circuit evaluation makes the operation faster, and, as shown in Lesson 3, is what makes guarded checks like `if (name != null && name.length() > 0)` safe.
